title: Observation data is not a local decision
summary: A dependency map connecting global climate observations, public radar products, national elevation design, transportation-risk synthesis, interpretation, local exposure, and decision records without treating data availability as an outcome.
map_question: What must happen after official observation data becomes available before FTFN can support a local climate, infrastructure, water, agriculture, or hazard decision claim?
interpretation_boundary: This map supports a sequence from observations to local decisions. It does not prove that a specific institution used the data, chose the correct model, funded an action, implemented it, or achieved a measurable outcome.

nodes.label: Official observations and surveys
nodes.note: NOAA, NASA, and USGS records provide climate, radar, elevation, mapping, and exploration observations with different scopes and maturities.

nodes.label: NOAA 2025 climate baseline
nodes.note: A dated global observation baseline that remains upstream of regional and local effects.

nodes.label: NISAR public radar data
nodes.note: An operating public-data rail with coverage, validation, model, adoption, and outcome work still downstream.

nodes.label: Next-generation 3DEP
nodes.note: A national program transition whose local coverage, quality, refresh, and use must be checked.

nodes.label: Coverage, calibration, version, and quality
nodes.note: A decision needs the correct product, geography, time period, resolution, version, method, and limitations.

nodes.label: Domain model and interpretation
nodes.note: Observations become sector evidence through validated models, ground truth, assumptions, and expert interpretation.

nodes.label: Named local assets and exposure
nodes.note: FTFN still needs local assets, exposure, vulnerability, decision authority, and outcome evidence before drawing local climate conclusions.

nodes.label: Documented decision and implementation
nodes.note: A plan, budget, permit, procurement, construction, operating change, or other authority record must show how evidence affected action.

nodes.label: Measured local outcome
nodes.note: Performance, losses, service, resilience, yield, water, safety, or other outcomes require their own records and counterfactual care.

links.note: NOAA supplies the official annual observation record.
NASA supplies an operating radar-data rail.
USGS defines the next acquisition and delivery model; local product status still varies.
Observation claims depend on inspectable data scope and quality.
Suitable data must be interpreted through validated domain methods.
Local meaning requires named assets, exposures, vulnerabilities, and authority.
Evidence matters only when a responsible institution documents a decision or action.
Implementation must be followed by operating and outcome evidence.

what_this_map_supports: Official observation availability can be separated from interpretation, institutional adoption, action, and outcome.
Climate, radar, elevation, and exploration records can share a common evidence-conversion stack without being treated as equivalent datasets.
Local climate and infrastructure claims require named exposure and authority records.
what_this_map_does_not_prove: It does not prove complete data coverage, correct model selection, local institutional use, funded implementation, causation, or measured benefit.
It does not convert global conditions into local forecasts or observed outcomes.
It does not score or rank local resilience.
next_records_needed: product-specific coverage, calibration, version, resolution, quality, and revision records.
regional models, ground truth, assumptions, uncertainty, and validation.
named local asset, hazard, exposure, vulnerability, and authority records.
plans, budgets, permits, procurements, construction, operating changes, and measured outcomes.
